summary: PROPOSED. D03 keeps the trunk's early mathematics, astronomy, calendars and measurement, and makes them causally honest and less tied to one tradition. (1) Research stage: algebra required geometry_axiomatic, so the stage's '(geometry_axiomatic OR algebra)' offered no real alternative: every path went through Greek deductive geometry. Algebra now requires a positional calculating system (hindu_arabic OR the new counting_rods) AND geometry_practical. That opens Indian/Islamic and Chinese routes, and both cost more than the Greek route, so no cost is softened. (2) The three calendar nodes were the only A1–A5 nodes scored institutional 3.0, the scale maximum otherwise used by A8–A9 national programmes and astrolabe. They are re-scored to their Age priors, each with a stated content reason: calendar_lunar 4,180 → 620, calendar_civil 5,910 → 1,760, calendar_lunisolar 3,520 → 1,240. (3) Causality and chronology: surveying's Mesopotamian branch named Old Babylonian arithmetic (~1,800 BCE), about seven centuries after Sumerian field surveying; it now names cuneiform (Group B). Practical geometry is re-dated from Thales to Bronze Age Egypt and Babylonia (A4 → A3, cost unchanged). Geometric astronomy now builds on the luni-solar period relations (calendar_lunisolar), which is no longer a dead end. Distillation accepts copper or bronze apparatus as an alternative to blown glass. Standard weights accept the Chinese record-keeping route. (4) Classification: four domesticates and pigment processing are re-filed under agriculture/materials, matching their peers. One new node (counting_rods); no split, merge or retirement. The two remaining dead ends carry a cross-lane request (water_clock) or an explicit justification (abacus).

existing.rationale: Historical re-anchoring. '~600 BCE Ionia' (Thales) dates the start of Greek deductive geometry, which is the prehistory of geometry_axiomatic. Area and volume computation is attested in Middle Kingdom Egypt (the Moscow papyrus, material ~1,850 BCE, with a frustum volume; the Rhind papyrus, copied ~1,550 BCE from a 12th-dynasty text) and in Old Babylonian mathematics (~1,800 BCE). The Sulba Sutras (India) and the Han Chinese classics came later. The Age metadata therefore moves A4 → A3, and difficulty and institutional take the A3 prior. Breadth rises because the node now underlies both deductive geometry and algebra. The two corrections happen to cancel, so the cost is unchanged.

existing.rationale: Causal prerequisite and anchor fix. Predictive geometric models need mean motions, and the Greeks took those from Babylonian calendrical astronomy. Hipparchus (as relayed by Ptolemy) used Babylonian eclipse records back to 721 BCE and long-period month relations. The 19-year luni-solar cycle (Babylon from ~499 BCE; Meton 432 BCE) underlies the Callippic and Hipparchic year and month lengths. The edge therefore runs through calendar_lunisolar, which still requires astronomy_records. The anchor adds Hipparchus, whose solar and lunar models came three centuries before the Almagest.

Factors unchanged: two conjuncts, so prereq_complexity stays 0.5. Capability block overridden.
existing.prereqRationale: geometry_axiomatic supplies the models (circles, epicycles, chords). calendar_lunisolar supplies the luni-solar period relations that fix their mean motions, and through it astronomy_records still supplies the observations. existing.rationale: Regional-material alternative. The alembic tradition did not depend on blown glass. Zosimos quotes Maria's instruction that the tubes be of copper or bronze, joints sealed with flour paste; glass was valued for watching reactions and for mercurial or sulphurous work. Copper and bronze stills are also known later, in the Islamic world and Jin–Yuan China (INFERENCE, not re-checked this session). Where later chemistry genuinely needs glass, the tree states it on those nodes: chemistry_quantitative requires barometer_vacuum, which requires glass_blowing. The acid nodes' vessels are D04's call; D04's part gives sulphuric_acid the lead-chamber route, 'distillation AND saltpetre_refining'. The early Gandhara ceramic 'stills' were not used as evidence: recent experimental work disputes them.

existing.rationale: Research-stage finding (culturally narrow). Because algebra required geometry_axiomatic, the stage atom '(geometry_axiomatic OR algebra)' offered no real alternative: every path to the stage held Greek axiomatic geometry. Al-Khwarizmi's geometric demonstrations drew on Euclid, but algebra itself did not need them. Brahmagupta (628 CE) gave rules for zero, negatives and the quadratic without Euclidean proof. The Chinese fangcheng (Nine Chapters) and Song–Yuan polynomial algebra (1247–1303 CE) grew from counting-rod computation. Algebra's causal requirements are a positional calculating system and the area-based problem tradition of practical geometry. The Indian/Islamic route (hindu_arabic) and the Chinese route (counting_rods) both cost more than the Greek route to the stage, so the stage is broadened without being made cheaper.

existing.prereqRationale: A positional system able to carry general computation (Indian numerals with zero, or Chinese counting rods), AND the area-and-measure problem tradition (geometry_practical) that algebra generalized in every centre. geometry_axiomatic is dropped because it encoded one tradition's justification, not a requirement. Every holder of the old prerequisite (hindu_arabic + geometry_axiomatic, hence geometry_practical) satisfies the new one, so availability only widens. calculus still requires geometry_axiomatic explicitly. openQuestions: OPEN DECISION (AI policy, not content). AiResearchPolicy closes goals over the union of every OR alternative (MEASURED in code, AiResearchPolicy.cs:184-195), so alternative routes become de facto mandatory for AI polities. INFERENCE from measurements/baseline-ai-node-completions.csv, seed 42: the AI completed abjad (658), brahmi (662) and hindu_arabic (684), 10,310 RP of the algebra branch, before geometry_axiomatic (710), and numeral_sexagesimal and arithmetic_babylonian (501/507) before surveying (522). Recommend closing each goal over its cheapest satisfying alternative, as tools/kr_lib.py's closure does. Every OR route this package adds on a goal path (e.g. counting_rods → algebra) otherwise costs AI polities RP.
